question: An operations coordinator notices a teammate pasting spreadsheets of customer names and order histories into a personal Claude account, even though the company provides a managed Claude for Work workspace. What should the coordinator do first?
options: A) Ask the teammate to delete those conversations, and treat the matter as closed once deletion is confirmed.
B) Post a general reminder about approved tools in the team channel so everyone is aware of the expectation.
C) Wait and see whether the practice continues, raising it only if customer data later appears in a shared file.
D) Raise it through the escalation path the company's AI policy defines for suspected data-handling problems.
correct_answers: D) Raise it through the escalation path the company's AI policy defines for suspected data-handling problems.
explanations: Deletion may be part of the remedy, but an individual arrangement bypasses the assessment and record the policy requires.
A general reminder does not address a specific incident that has already put customer data outside the managed workspace.
Waiting leaves an active exposure unreported and makes the eventual review harder, since the extent will be larger.
Correct. Customer data has already left the approved environment, and the policy's escalation path exists precisely so this is assessed by the people accountable for it.
